analysis.AN_Notes: Survey and taxonomy of intersectional fairness notions and mitigation in ML. Gender and race are the worked axes (Figure 1, Black women example); disability, religion, socioeconomic status appear in single cited works or dataset tables. Harm types structuring the synthesis: accuracy and worst-case performance gaps of intersectional subgroups (Disparate_Performance) and outcome-ratio notions derived from the 80 percent disparate-impact rule (Indirect_Discrimination by the YMABYPKF anchor); the survey itself does not classify direct versus indirect discrimination. Mitigation stages from the taxonomy: dataset coverage for intersectional groups (Pre_Processing), in-processing DRO, adversarial reweighting and auditing games (In_Training), multicalibration boosting and prediction flipping (Post_Processing). Evaluated is a synthesised status from reported experimental results of cited methods, not an own experiment. Gender is handled as a categorical attribute ('male/female for a binary gender'). Feministisch ja rests on Crenshaw's intersectionality as the core concept; Gender teilweise because gender is one component axis of an intersectional fairness survey. AI Agent Review: Organisational_Process is added for the recommended involvement of diverse stakeholders in designing fairness notions (sections 2.7 and 6).
